statement: The NDC reports a 17-30% rainfall decline in 1900-2018, with different temperature trends on the plateau and coast.
compact_statement: The NDC reports a 17-30% rainfall decline in 1900-2018, with different temperature trends on the plateau and coast.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 40, section 4.2, observed rainfall and temperature changes

statement: NDC presents RCP2.6/RCP8.5 projections against 1986-2006, including 2030/2050 precipitation maps.
compact_statement: NDC presents RCP2.6/RCP8.5 projections against 1986-2006, including 2030/2050 precipitation maps.
uncertainty: Projection scope only; no magnitude asserted.

statement: Consultation ranks farmers, pastoralists, rural residents, fishers and urban poor among groups most vulnerable to climate impacts.
compact_statement: Consultation ranks farmers, pastoralists, rural residents, fishers and urban poor among groups most vulnerable to climate impacts.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 40–41, section 4.2, vulnerability ranking from survey and stakeholder consultation

uncertainty: Consultation ranking, not measured household risk.

statement: NDC reports three major droughts in the prior 30 years and water constraints from low rainfall, few permanent rivers and insufficient storage.
compact_statement: NDC reports three major droughts in the prior 30 years and water constraints from low rainfall, few permanent rivers and insufficient storage.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 42, section 4.2, water and agriculture vulnerability

uncertainty: The period is relative to NDC publication.

statement: NDC identifies 23 land-degradation hotspots (9.8% of Eritrea) and reports crop-variety loss, pests and livestock deaths among drought concerns.
compact_statement: NDC identifies 23 land-degradation hotspots (9.8% of Eritrea) and reports crop-variety loss, pests and livestock deaths among drought concerns.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 42, section 4.2, agriculture impacts and land-degradation hotspots

uncertainty: Prior assessment; other land-use drivers are not isolated.

statement: UNDP cites about 500,000 cultivated hectares, 93% rain-fed, and says low, erratic rainfall and land degradation expose rural communities to drought risks.
compact_statement: UNDP cites about 500,000 cultivated hectares, 93% rain-fed, and says low, erratic rainfall and land degradation expose rural communities to drought risks.

source_refs.locator: ‘In depth’ section, paragraphs on agriculture and rural communities

uncertainty: Undated UNDP page attributes cultivated-area and irrigation figures to Ministry of Agriculture 2022.

statement: The proposal reports that seasonal Anseba River baseflow lasted only a few months and groundwater lay 2–3 m below the stream, constraining local water access.
compact_statement: The proposal reports that seasonal Anseba River baseflow lasted only a few months and groundwater lay 2–3 m below the stream, constraining local water access.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Anseba regional project context, Hamelmalo and Habero

uncertainty: Proposal describes conditions at preparation time; its receipt date is blank and the baseline should not be read as current.

statement: The proposal identifies possible increased social conflict over water and land as a secondary risk of climate-related livelihood stress.
compact_statement: The proposal identifies possible increased social conflict over water and land as a secondary risk of climate-related livelihood stress.
affected_groups: people dependent on land and water
scenario: The inspected summary does not specify it.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 3, project background, climate impacts on livelihoods

uncertainty: A project proposal’s prospective risk statement, not an observed or causal estimate; the passage gives no timeframe or conflict measurement.

statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: At five consulted project sites, dams, diversions and water-harvesting structures still supported irrigation, pastoralism and hygiene; siltation and maintenance problems limited sustainability.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: At five consulted project sites, dams, diversions and water-harvesting structures still supported irrigation, pastoralism and hygiene; siltation and maintenance problems limited sustainability.
uncertainty: Selected visited sites, not region-wide coverage.

statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: Ministry-led MIHAP replication sustained agricultural diversification and livestock production; Anseba authorities reported 58 of 640 participating households became small or medium commercial enterprises.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: Ministry-led MIHAP replication sustained agricultural diversification and livestock production; Anseba authorities reported 58 of 640 participating households became small or medium commercial enterprises.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 3, Outcome 2 findings and regional-authority data

uncertainty: The 640-household figure is from regional authorities; some benefits were beneficiary-reported.

statement: The ex-post evaluation observed three of six hydromet stations: all three generated data, but two had partial functionality. Data were not centrally automated and farm advice was uneven.
compact_statement: The ex-post evaluation observed three of six hydromet stations: all three generated data, but two had partial functionality. Data were not centrally automated and farm advice was uneven.
uncertainty: Only three stations observed; do not infer all six were functioning or that the network delivered systematic warnings.

statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: The evaluation found women’s participation and leadership sustained after the project; women reported reduced water-fetching burdens, and children’s school attendance improved.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-01-28 reports: The evaluation found women’s participation and leadership sustained after the project; women reported reduced water-fetching burdens, and children’s school attendance improved.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 5, contribution to local resilience

uncertainty: Selected project-site evaluation contributions and stakeholder reports, not measured peace outcomes or controlled effects on school attendance.

statement: Source dated 2002 reports: After the border war disrupted transhumance and Tekezze-Setit basin watering access, herds shifted to wells around Goluj and nearby return sites; the study reports emerging farmer–livestock-owner conflict.
compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: After the border war disrupted transhumance and Tekezze-Setit basin watering access, herds shifted to wells around Goluj and nearby return sites; the study reports emerging farmer–livestock-owner conflict.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 24–25, returnee impacts perceived by Goluj residents

uncertainty: Exceptional localized 1999–2001 post-war access constraints/tensions around Goluj, not current insecurity, climate-caused conflict or a general claim about returnees.

statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Rapid borehole development in Gash-Barka changed water use and encouraged larger livestock populations; the study cautioned that resource pressure could threaten poor returnee and stayee livelihoods.
compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Rapid borehole development in Gash-Barka changed water use and encouraged larger livestock populations; the study cautioned that resource pressure could threaten poor returnee and stayee livelihoods.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 1–2, executive-summary findings on returnee water provision and resource use

uncertainty: Historical resource-use changes and prospective pressure, not climate attribution or inevitable conflict.

statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Around Goluj, respondents linked scarcer fuelwood to population-related forest depletion; poor households lacking transport or money reduced use, while animal owners could access markets.
compact_statement: Source dated 2002 reports: Around Goluj, respondents linked scarcer fuelwood to population-related forest depletion; poor households lacking transport or money reduced use, while animal owners could access markets.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 20–21, fuelwood availability, access and household response

uncertainty: Historical household survey and interviews; findings concern sampled communities.

statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: UNDP’s case study reports erratic below-average rain in 2002–2004, especially in parts of Habero, caused livestock losses and impaired livelihoods; annual rain ranged from 190 mm in Habero to about 367 mm in Hamelmalo.
compact_statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: UNDP’s case study reports erratic below-average rain in 2002–2004, especially in parts of Habero, caused livestock losses and impaired livelihoods; annual rain ranged from 190 mm in Habero to about 367 mm in Hamelmalo.

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 2–3 (one-based), Anseba climate and livelihood context

uncertainty: Historical project-preparation context, not a recent rainfall assessment.

statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: Anseba herders moved west in July–September and toward the eastern escarpment or Northern Red Sea in November–March; land-use pressure, degradation and settlement policies disrupted this practice.
compact_statement: Source dated 2012-11 reports: Anseba herders moved west in July–September and toward the eastern escarpment or Northern Red Sea in November–March; land-use pressure, degradation and settlement policies disrupted this practice.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2 (one-based), Anseba pastoral movements and land-use context

uncertainty: The case study lists multiple pressures and policies; it does not isolate their effects.

statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For solar-asset planning, GCA describes lowland and coastal rainfall below 100 mm with dry spells over 200 days, versus wetter highlands; drought hazard is very high across most Eritrea and dust/wind risk is elevated in Anseba.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For solar-asset planning, GCA describes lowland and coastal rainfall below 100 mm with dry spells over 200 days, versus wetter highlands; drought hazard is very high across most Eritrea and dust/wind risk is elevated in Anseba.
uncertainty: GCA summarizes modelled climatology and high-level asset hazards, not local household impacts.

statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For 2030–2060, mean annual rainfall is projected to fall by up to 100 mm on the Eritrean Plateau, with slight increases in western lowlands and southern areas; wet-day changes are small under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-03 reports: For 2030–2060, mean annual rainfall is projected to fall by up to 100 mm on the Eritrean Plateau, with slight increases in western lowlands and southern areas; wet-day changes are small under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
uncertainty: The source notes high climate-model uncertainty; the chapter is not a general social-risk assessment.
